item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Blue Wahoos have announced plans to bring Banana Ball to the city next year, with two games scheduled for 2027. Banana Ball is an exhibition baseball format known for its fast-paced, entertainment-focused gameplay and fan-friendly rules.

The Blue Wahoos, a Double-A affiliate of the Cincinnati Reds that plays at Pensacola's Community Maritime Park, regularly host special events and exhibitions alongside their regular minor-league season. The announcement adds to the team's event calendar and represents another draw for local baseball fans looking for something different from traditional ballpark fare.

Banana Ball games have been part of a touring exhibition circuit that emphasizes entertainment value, including shorter games and modified rules designed to increase action and fan engagement. Details about specific dates and ticket information were not immediately available.

item.content:encoded:
The Tate Aggies and Northview Chiefs both saw their district tournament runs end Friday night in volleyball action across the area.

Tate, seeded No. 3 in the District 1-5A tournament, fell to No. 2 seed Niceville in straight sets during Friday's semifinal matchup at Niceville. The Eagles' sweep ended the Aggies' postseason hopes in the district tournament.

Northview also bowed out of tournament play Friday, though specific details of that match were not immediately available. Both teams now turn their attention to potential playoff qualification or consolation bracket opportunities depending on their district standings.

Saturday will be sunny with a high near 69 degrees, but the gusty winds are expected to persist. The combination of dry…
item.content:encoded:
A wind advisory remains in effect across portions of the Florida Panhandle including the North Escambia area, with strong gusts expected to create an enhanced threat for downed trees and power outages through the weekend.

Saturday will be sunny with a high near 69 degrees, but the gusty winds are expected to persist. The combination of dry conditions and strong winds has also elevated wildfire risk across the region on Saturday, according to the forecast.

Residents should secure loose outdoor items and be prepared for potential power disruptions. Motorists should exercise caution, particularly on bridges and in open areas where wind gusts can be strongest.

item.title: DeSantis Details Storm Recovery Push for Panhandle, Eyes Federal Aid
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis highlighted ongoing relief efforts across the Florida Panhandle during a press conference in Milton, outlining a coordinated state response to storm damage in the region. According to reporting on the event, DeSantis discussed the distribution of emergency resources to affected areas, an expedited request for federal disaster…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis highlighted ongoing relief efforts across the Florida Panhandle during a press conference in Milton, outlining a coordinated state response to storm damage in the region.

According to reporting on the event, DeSantis discussed the distribution of emergency resources to affected areas, an expedited request for federal disaster declaration status, and a new state partnership that will deploy travel trailers to help displaced homeowners rebuild. The governor's visit underscores the scale of recovery work facing inland communities throughout the Panhandle following recent severe weather.

The relief push combines state resources with federal coordination, aiming to accelerate assistance for residents dealing with property damage and displacement across the region.

The Pensacola Blue Wahoos announced they will host two Banana Ball games in 2027, bringing the entertainment-focused baseball spectacle to the Emerald Coast.

Banana Ball is the signature brand of baseball created by the Savannah Bananas, known for fast-paced games, creative promotions, and a high-energy fan experience that differs sharply from traditional Major League Baseball. The Bananas have built a national following with their unique style of play and showmanship.

According to WKRG News 5, the Blue Wahoos will welcome the Bananas for two games next season. Details on dates, ticket information, and specific game times have not yet been released by the team.

item.content:encoded:
The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority board accepted Executive Director Jason Yarborough's resignation during a special meeting Friday, according to a statement from ECUA's Public Information Office.

Bruce Woody, former ECUA executive director, will step into the role of acting executive director while the authority conducts a search for a permanent replacement, ECUA said.

No details were provided about the circumstances of Yarborough's departure or a timeline for the executive director search.

item.title: DeSantis Appoints Naples Building Official to State Construction Board

Beckman currently serves as director of Building Services for the City of Naples and holds multiple certifications including General Contractor, Building Code Administrator, and Plans Examiner through the Florida Department of…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced Friday the appointment of Stephen Beckman to the Construction Industry Licensing Board. Beckman currently serves as director of Building Services for the City of Naples and holds multiple certifications including General Contractor, Building Code Administrator, and Plans Examiner through the Florida Department of Business Regulation.

Beckman is active in professional organizations, including the Building Officials Association of Florida and the Association of State Floodplain Managers. He earned his bachelor's degree from Concordia College.

The appointment is subject to confirmation by the Florida Senate, according to the Governor's Press Office.

item.title: Milton prioritizes school bus stops for debris removal ahead of reopening
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The City of Milton is focusing storm debris removal efforts around school bus stops and campuses as Santa Rosa County schools prepare to reopen next week following Hurricane Isaias, according to a city news release issued Friday. Crew began collection operations Tuesday, October 13, and are working daily through November to clear an estimated…
item.content:encoded:
The City of Milton is focusing storm debris removal efforts around school bus stops and campuses as Santa Rosa County schools prepare to reopen next week following Hurricane Isaias, according to a city news release issued Friday.

Crew began collection operations Tuesday, October 13, and are working daily through November to clear an estimated 400,000 cubic yards of storm debris plus another 35,000 cubic yards of construction and demolition material. Residents may notice debris trucks in neighborhoods collecting some piles while leaving others — the city says crews are prioritizing school-related access first and will return for additional collection as operations progress.

Parents and guardians should keep children closely supervised near bus stops and debris work zones. The city warns of active heavy equipment, utility crews, and recovery activities in neighborhoods. The debris processing site is located about three blocks from Rhodes Elementary School at Byrom and James Streets, where motorists and pedestrians should exercise caution.

Preliminary damage assessments show about 60% of Milton structures sustained some storm damage, with roughly 5% deemed uninhabitable. The city asked residents to remain patient as recovery continues.

item.title: Pensacola State College resuming normal operations Monday after weather closure
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Pensacola State College will return to normal operations on Monday, October 19, following a weather-related closure that affected the campus this week. All classes, events, and activities will resume, according to a media alert from the college. College officials say all facilities have been inspected and deemed safe for occupancy, with one…
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola State College will return to normal operations on Monday, October 19, following a weather-related closure that affected the campus this week. All classes, events, and activities will resume, according to a media alert from the college.

College officials say all facilities have been inspected and deemed safe for occupancy, with one exception: the Milton Campus Library will remain closed pending repairs. Employees at that location will report to the Pensacola Campus Library instead, while all other staff will return to their regular work stations.

Fall B session final exams are scheduled for Monday and Tuesday (October 19-20), and Fall D session classes begin Monday. The college's Drop and Add period for D session concludes Tuesday. Faculty have been asked to extend deadlines and due dates for coursework and exams affected by the closure, and to remain flexible as campus operations ramp back up.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Libraries Reopen Monday After Hurricane Closures
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Three branches of the Santa Rosa County Library System will resume service Monday, October 19, following temporary closures caused by a recent hurricane. The Jay, Pace, and Gulf Breeze libraries will reopen during their regularly scheduled hours, while the Library Administration office will also resume operations. The reopened locations will offer…
item.content:encoded:
Three branches of the Santa Rosa County Library System will resume service Monday, October 19, following temporary closures caused by a recent hurricane. The Jay, Pace, and Gulf Breeze libraries will reopen during their regularly scheduled hours, while the Library Administration office will also resume operations.

The reopened locations will offer additional computer access to help residents navigate hurricane recovery—allowing community members to research assistance programs, complete online forms, and access critical information during the rebuilding effort.

Two other facilities remain closed. The Navarre Library continues experiencing storm-related power problems, while the Milton Library's previously planned October 19 reopening—originally scheduled after renovations—has been postponed to Monday, October 26 due to hurricane-related delays. The Family History & Research Center will remain closed until further notice as the county assesses conditions across the system.

Santa Rosa County Communications said staff will announce additional reopening dates as facilities are restored. Residents can call (850) 981-7323 or visit www.santarosa.fl.gov/libraries for updates.

The all-clear comes after water quality samples met safety requirements, allowing residents to use tap water normally again without boiling it…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County officials have rescinded the boil water notice for the Town of Jay as of Friday afternoon, following completion of bacteriological testing that confirmed the water supply is safe to drink.

The all-clear comes after water quality samples met safety requirements, allowing residents to use tap water normally again without boiling it first.

Meanwhile, boil water notices remain in effect for all customers of Bagdad Garcon Point Water. Residents in affected areas should continue to boil water before drinking or using it for cooking until they receive notice that their local system has been cleared.

item.title: Sen. Rick Scott visits Cyprus to discuss Mediterranean security, energy ties
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senator Rick Scott traveled to Cyprus today as part of a diplomatic visit focused on strengthening U.S. interests in the Mediterranean region. Scott, who chairs the Senate Armed Services Subcommittee on Seapower and sits on the Foreign Relations Committee, met with U.S. Ambassador John Breslow and Cypriot Energy, Commerce, and Industry…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott traveled to Cyprus today as part of a diplomatic visit focused on strengthening U.S. interests in the Mediterranean region. Scott, who chairs the Senate Armed Services Subcommittee on Seapower and sits on the Foreign Relations Committee, met with U.S. Ambassador John Breslow and Cypriot Energy, Commerce, and Industry Minister Michael Damianos to discuss expanding energy infrastructure between Europe and the Middle East.

During the visit, Scott toured the United Nations Buffer Zone that divides the island, reaffirming U.S. support for Cypriot sovereignty and calling out Turkish military occupation that has persisted since 1974. "A strong, reunified Cyprus makes it easier to do business in the region and counters the aggression we've seen from thugs like Putin and Erdogan," Scott said in a statement, noting that Turkey remains the principal obstacle to resolving the island's division.

Scott emphasized the strategic importance of a stable Mediterranean as the U.S. energy industry expands its presence in the region and energy flows between the Middle East and Europe increase. He called on Cyprus and other regional allies to strengthen their defenses to reduce reliance on U.S. military involvement overseas.

item.content:encoded: Fairhope Police Department officers have determined that a bomb threat reported in the area was actually a swatting call, according to WKRG-TV 5. Swatting incidents involve false emergency reports designed to send armed police response teams to a specific location, often as a prank or harassment tactic. The confirmation came after officers investigated the initial report and ruled out any credible threat.
